A '''sequence''' is an ordered collection of distinct '''elements'''.

An unordered collection of distinct elements is referred to as a [[set]].

== Formal definition ==

Let $S\ne \emptyset$ be a [[set]].

Any function 

$$
A:\mathbb{N} \to S
$$

is a '''sequence'''.

== Subsequence ==

If $a_{n_i} \in (a_n)$, then

$$
(a_{n_i}) \subset (a_n)
$$

$(a_{n_i})$ is hence known as a subsequence of $(a_n)$.
